question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 17 hours, pipe B can fill the same tank in 24 hours and pipe C can fill the same tank in 18 hours. The time taken by them to fill the same tank if they operate together is::
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = **LCM** of filling times = **LCM(17, 24, 18)** = 17 × 72 = **1224 units**.

Combined Efficiency = (1224 ÷ 17) + (1224 ÷ 24) + (1224 ÷ 18) = 72 + 51 + 68 = **191 units/hr**.

Time Taken = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency = 1224 ÷ 191 = **6(78/191) hours**.

**∴ The correct answer is 6(78/191) hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Combined Work Formula

For three pipes filling a tank, the total time T is given by 1/T = 1/t₁ + 1/t₂ + 1/t₃.

Pipes and Cisterns Efficiency

Filling pipes have positive efficiency, while outlet (leakage) pipes have negative efficiency.

LCM Method

Total capacity of the tank is assumed as the LCM of the individual times to simplify calculations into integers.</p
